name: Microcornea-Posterior Megalolenticonus-Persistent Fetal Vasculature-Coloboma Syndrome
aliases: Microcornea with Posterior Megalolenticonus and Persistent Fetal Vasculature Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Microcornea-Posterior Megalolenticonus-Persistent Fetal Vasculature-Coloboma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of microcornea defined as corneal diameter less than 10 mm in neonates
Posterior megalolenticonus characterized by abnormal enlargement and deformation of the posterior lens capsule
Evidence of persistent fetal vasculature (PFV) on ocular examination or imaging
Presence of ocular coloboma affecting iris, retina, or optic nerve

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires presence of microcornea, posterior megalolenticonus, persistent fetal vasculature, and ocular coloboma.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by ophthalmological imaging.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Remnants of the hyaloid vascular system
searchTerms: remnants of hyaloid vessels in eye

imaging: Ocular ultrasound showing persistent fetal vasculature
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography demonstrating microcornea and lens abnormalities
Fundus photography revealing coloboma and retinal changes
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected sporadic or unknown genetic etiology
other: Clinical ophthalmological examination revealing characteristic features

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated persistent fetal vasculature without coloboma
Coloboma without microcornea or lens abnormalities

redFlags: Severe congenital visual impairment or blindness
Progressive glaucoma or retinal detachment risk
